company: HSIE Results Daily: Oil India, Amber Enterprises
headline: HSIE Results Daily: Oil India, Amber Enterprises-2QFY27

highlights: Q2FY27 standalone EBITDA of INR 30bn (+126.5% YoY, -26.5% QoQ) and APAT of INR 22.5bn (+116.4% YoY, -21.3% QoQ) came in below our estimates.

Q2 crude sales stood at 0.98 MMT (+18.4% YoY, +7.0% QoQ) and gas sales at 0.66 bcm (-0.6% YoY, +6.5% QoQ). ■ Amber Enterprises: Amber’s Q2FY27 revenue grew 60% YoY (2-yr CAGR: 25%) to INR 26.3bn on a low base, mainly due to strong performance in the electronics segment.
Consumer durables segment grew by 41% YoY, electronics grew by 94% YoY, and railways delivered 15% growth YoY.
EBITDAM declined by 180bps YoY to 3.7% (-430bps QoQ), leading to 8% YoY EBITDA growth (2-year CAGR -7%), while APAT stood at INR -706mn vs INR -329mn YoY.
valuation: We maintain REDUCE with a lower target price of INR 7,230/share, based on a DCF valuation (WACC: 12%, terminal growth: 5%), implying ~38x Sep-28E EPS.
Capex is INR 75bn/INR 60bn for FY27/FY28E. ■ Change in estimates and valuation: We cut FY27E EPS by 5.1%, mainly to reflect NRL's weaker Q2 GRM.
The company noted an inventory valuation impact of INR 288mn in H1, with further impact of INR 320mn expected in H2.
watch: We expect gas to start flowing through the NRL-IGGL link by Jan 2027; full connectivity is 18-20 months away. ■ Key takeaways: (1) The board recommended interim dividend of INR 7 per share of INR10 each.

The views herein are of a general nature and do not consider the risk appetite or the particular circumstances of an individual investor; readers are requested to take professional advice before investing. “This report may have been refined using AI tools to enhance clarity and readability.” Nothing in this document should be construed as investment advice.
